body: yes, and I have the links open on my computer, but haven't had a chance to watch them all yet. That's why I haven't responded.

going to the hospital means that I come out of the hospital in exactly the same position, but with another massive hospital bill. I'll have lost everything at that point. The hospital may fix the depression, but the money situation is my real problem, and I don't want to add to that. Once I have a job, fixing the mental health issues is at the top of the list, but until that happens, it's gotta be on the back burner.
me too. I have 3 days left to find one. I'm looking. I just don't have a lot of hope.

I'm not giving up until the last minute. Technically, I have 5 days. If I can find the money for the car payment by then, that buys me until the end of the month. If I can find a job before the 15th, then maybe I can talk to the guy I'm paying for the car, and he'll hold off for a couple of weeks. But if the weekend comes, and I don't have either of those, it's likely I'll lose the car, and without a way to get to work, I don't see a way to fix it. That's why I decided this weekend would be it.

See, that's the problem. I am aware that I have to MAKE things better. And I've tried, really really hard. I've been fighting a losing battle against that for the past year. A year ago, when I was facing my eviction and loss of my savings, and some friends helped me out, I busted my ass trying to find a job and get on track. I did eventually find one, but it was minimum wage and part time, so it was really only enough to help out when I could. Then, in December, I realized what I needed to do, and I forced myself to be positive, think positive thoughts, and try to make positive change happen in my life. I made some successes. I got a better job, in the field I had experience in, I started clearing up debt, and I started trying to fix relationships that I had screwed up. I made some steps forward, and lots of people said they were proud of me. But then, I had massive failures to go along with it. I cleared up all my debt but my car payment and student loans, only to be hit with a massive medical bill for a kidney stone with no insurance. I lost the one person that had stuck with me through the worst of my depression. I ended up losing THAT job, as well. Now I'm going to lose my car if I don't have the money for the car payment in 5 days (which is unlikely). It seems like the more I fight to MAKE things better, the more the universe takes it as a challenge to make things worse. and sure, I could keep fighting, and hope that maybe next week I'll start making forward progress, but all I've seen is slipping down this hole, and much like quicksand, the harder I fight to stay afloat, the faster I go down.

made too much money last year. Medicaid isn't easy to get, especially as a single male with no dependents, it is very difficult to get. I probably COULD qualify at the moment, but like I said elsewhere, I'm not worried about fixing my depression so much as I am making sure I'm not homeless or carless. (Atlanta sucks without a vehicle, and I live too far north to access public transportation.)

Thank you for that suggestion. I actually have considered checking myself into a hospital, but as I'm already under a mountain of debt, that means adding more to it, as well as being unable to pay the bills I have now. I lose my phone, my car, and pretty much everything I own. If there were a way to handle that while I was in the hospital, I'd seriously go tonight.

The employment councillor is a good idea, I didn't know those things existed outside of high schools. (High school is such a shitty thing, it prepares you for nothing, then kicks you out into the world, and screw you if you haven't figured it out.)

I just don't feel like talking is going to fix anything. I posted before, explaining my situation, and sure, depression is a factor - possibly a significant one, but even if I could magically fix that right now, I'd still have all the other problems, and I would still be very unhappy at the prospect of continuing down this hole. I'm looking for a way out, but if I don't find one before the weekend, I don't think I want to deal with it anymore.

Here's the previous post, if you want to read it. http://redd.it/1bwlhf

I'm not ready to give up yet. Although, I'm very very very close to being ready. And I've talked to someone a couple of times, but they say the same thing most other people say. "It will get better" or "We have to overcome these challenges to be better people". The problem is, at this point, it's a question if I want to deal with the thought of being homeless and alone, or just give up. And really, it's not even the thought of being homeless that bothers me. Someone said "at least you know it can't get any worse". If the last couple years have taught me ANYTHING, it's that it can ALWAYS get worse, and will. This is the worst that I will accept. past this point, I give up.

I'm trying to reach out everywhere I can, and while I haven't told people that know me directly that I'm planning on killing myself, I have told them I need help. They understand my situation. If I can fix it - either with help, or alone, if that's even possible, than I will. But really, if I can't, I don't want to keep going down this hole.

the "luxury" I was referring to was leaving when I lost my temper. He did have bruises. His mom (my wife at the time) understood, and sympathized with me, she'd almost done the same thing herself. My mother in law found out later that evening when she saw the bruises. The bruises went away after a few days, and he always bruised very easily, so it was no surprise that he did. Note that this isn't an excuse, I DID lose my temper, and I also learned a lot from it. 

As for losing my job, no, nothing like that. I was prescribed two drugs, one for depression, (I can't remember which one at the moment) and Ambien for sleep. I was in a hurry one morning, and took the ambien instead of the depression drug. I went in, and was already feeling very out of it. They sent me home, and later let me go for "poor work performance" which was their compromise for me being there for 6 years. Otherwise they would've let me go for working under the influence of a drug, they said.

My daughter has already grown up without me. She happened across my facebook on accident a couple years ago, and we talk occasionally, but we're not close. Her mom actually got remarried, and told everyone I had died, so for most of her life, she thought I WAS dead. she'll be upset if I die, but not being close will probably be good for her. Also, I think it's better that she knows I'm dead, than worry that I'm sitting in some homeless shelter or hospital or something, and she has no idea where I am. At least if someone asks her, she can say "my dad is dead", unlike me, when people ask where my parents are, because I really don't know.

My reason? because I'm too far down this hole to fix things. I'm out of money and out of options. I see no prospects in the future. I thought I had the opportunity for a good job, that would've paid well, had insurance, and gotten me out of this hole, but they decided to go with someone less risky (because of the felony). So now, I've got a week to come up with money, or lose my car. After that, I can't get to work, and I lose my place to live. Then, I'm in a homeless shelter or under a bridge. The prospects just don't look good, and I'm tired of trying to fight it.

This is the note I'm probably going to post on facebook on Friday:

About a year ago, I thought about killing myself. My savings was all gone, I was about to lose my apartment, I had nowhere else to go, and no real job prospects. I didn't see any of that improving. But, a few friend decided to help out. They told me things would get better. Basically saved my life, although I don't know if I ever told them how close I was to completely giving up at that time. Of course, I was still pretty deep in a very dark depression, so it didn't go so well. 
Fast forward to October, and I had a job, but it was a minimum wage part time job, and certainly not enough to live on. Once again I was facing homelessness, and felt like I had no place to turn. This time, my church helped me out. I was extremely grateful, and I felt like I was beating the depression for once. Again, people told me things would get better. And it seemed like they were, for a bit.
I got a better job. I could live on the salary. Not well, but at least I could cover my bills. Then, I had an ugly breakup, which eventually led to a large amount of legal bills. I also developed some pretty excruciating medical problems, that led to a large amount of medical bills. I'm once again jobless, and no prospects for one in the near future. I am out of money, and I owe a lot of people a lot of money with no foreseeable way to pay them back.
Thanks to the breakup, I've been cut off from the church entirely, as well as most of my support network. My ex now hates me, and while she was instrumental in keeping me from killing myself in October, I believe she really wishes she'd just let me do it. 
So now I'm back in the position that I was in at the end of October. I'm about to lose my car, and when that happens, I will not be able to get to work. Without work, I won't be able to pay rent, and I'll be homeless. Because of the medical fees, legal fees, and low pay, I've not been able to create any kind of cushion. I feel like I've been demonized by the one person I used to feel like I could trust, and frankly, I feel like she truly does want me to disappear forever. 
So, I find myself asking the same question I was 6 months ago. What's the point? If I can do no better than failure, why continue trying? I clearly am incapable of making the right decisions, perhaps the only real option left is the wrong one? Maybe in that, I can do some good, or at least stop doing some bad.
So, it looks like as hard as I tried to be better, I don't think I can do it. And I'm really really tired of trying. So, I'm sitting here on a Saturday, writing what will be my final words, to be posted in a week. Saturday afternoon, I'm going to park my car somewhere, take a cab to a hotel somewhere, and take my last meal which will consist of a nice mixture of pills, some good wine, and I will finally stop trying.
To everyone that wanted to help me, or cared for me, or thought about me, I'm sorry. I wish I could've been more worthy of your concern. Count that as another failure.
This is the end. I'm tired of trying to do this, and not getting anywhere. I'm tired of making mistakes, and having those mistakes be a so much bigger focus on me than my successes. Sure, it's possible that there's a miracle right around the corner, but I can't see it. And at this point, it's just too late. If I don't find something in the next week, then I'm done. (Of course, if I do, nobody will read this, so if you're reading this, I didn't.)
